# Agent runtime (`runtime/`)

`@app-vitals/agent-runtime` is the agent process: it boots in a container,
pulls its configuration from the admin API, and then turns Slack messages, chat
messages and cron fires into `claude -p` sessions. It imports no specialty
code; specialty behavior arrives through the extension seam below.

Canonical sources this doc does not repeat: `runtime/package.json` (the
`exports` map), `runtime/Dockerfile` (image layout and the base-image
contract), and the admin API docs (`docs/agent-api.md`).

## Two processes

| Process | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Entrypoint | `entrypoint-main.ts` → `entrypoint.ts` | Container `ENTRYPOINT`. One-shot startup, then spawns the server and exits with its exit code. |
| Agent server | repo-root `index.ts` → `boot.ts` (`startAgent`) | Long-lived. Owns the single health server, Slack, the chat poller and the cron scheduler. |

The entrypoint must not start a health server: the server process binds the
port (`DEFAULT_HEALTH_PORT`, 3459) and a second listener would crash it with
`EADDRINUSE`.

### Entrypoint sequence

`runEntrypoint(deps)` takes every side effect as an injected dependency, so
tests pass doubles and production wires real ones in `entrypoint-main.ts`.

1. Require `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ID`, `SHIPWRIGHT_API_URL`, `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_API_KEY`
   (or `--agent-id`, `--api-url`, `--api-key`, parsed by `cli-args.ts`). Missing
   values log a fatal line and exit 1.
2. Fetch the config bundle (`GET /agents/:id/config`, via
   `shipwright-runtime-client.ts`).
3. Apply the bundle's `env` to `process.env` through `applyEnvToProcess`
   (`anthropic-federation-guard.ts` skips the Anthropic credential keys when
   workload-identity federation is active). `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_TYPE` is set from
   the bundle's `specialty`.
4. Symlink `~/.claude` to `$AGENT_HOME/dot-claude` (`ensureDotClaudeSymlink`).
5. GitHub auth (`setup-github-auth.ts`, below).
6. `runMiseStartup`: install the workspace's mise tools and put the shims on `PATH`.
7. `installPlugins` with the bundle's plugins, plus any marketplaces baked into
   the image under `/opt/shipwright/marketplaces` (`BAKED_MARKETPLACES_ROOT`).
8. Spawn `bun run index.ts` with inherited stdio.

Steps 2 to 8 race a deadline (180 s, overridable with
`SHIPWRIGHT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`). `mise install` on a cold node can be slow, so
keep the default aligned with the startup probe in `admin/src/agent-manifest.ts`.

## Boot order (`boot.ts`)

`startAgent(extensions)` runs these in order. The health server comes first so
kubelet probes stay green during setup.

1. `ensureAgentHome` creates `workspace/` (with `state/`, `repos/`,
   `worktrees/`, `.claude/`), `mise/`, and seeds the `*.md.template` files from
   `runtime/workspace/` (or the specialty's `identity.templatesDir`, see
   `resolveTemplatesDir`). Seeding never overwrites an existing file.
2. Health server.
3. `runMiseStartup` and `installPlugins` defaults.
4. First config sync (awaited), then repeated every 60 s: fetch the bundle,
   re-apply env, update the live Claude config, repos and policy refs, install
   plugins, clone newly configured repos, and start Slack if credentials have
   appeared.
5. `reconcileSystemCrons`, best effort and non-fatal.
6. Cron sync loop (60 s) and the periodic reconciler tick.
7. Slack Socket Mode app, chat poller, session pruner.

Three hooks wired in `boot.ts` ride on the config sync and are gated by the
bundle's `features` object (held in `agent-features-ref.ts`; absent means all
off):

- `transcriptUploader` uploads a redacted cron-run transcript after
  `completeRun` when `features.transcriptUpload` is true.
- `repoAccessProbe` probes per-repo GitHub access for the installations
  reporter when `features.repoAccessCheck` is true.
- `createRunNowHonourer` runs a cron job once on each sync tick when the admin
  has stamped a fresh `runRequestedAt`; jobs classified as `loop` go through
  `extension.dispatchLoop`.

See `agent-key-files.md` for each module's contract.
8. Graceful shutdown on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`.

Slack is optional. With no `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`/`SLACK_APP_TOKEN` the agent runs
chat-only, and `slack-startup.ts` (`startSlackIfPossible`) starts Bolt exactly
once whenever a later config sync supplies the credentials.

## Configuration

`createConfig(agentHome)` (`config.ts`) reads `process.env` at call time and
returns `claude`, `shipwright`, `slack`, `alerts`, `owner`, `voice`, `chat`
and `paths` groups. `AGENT_HOME` defaults to `/data/agent-home` in `boot.ts`.

### Voice (STT/TTS)

`config.voice` is a boot-time snapshot, used only to validate `PIPER_VOICE` at
startup. Synthesis and transcription instead call `buildVoiceConfig()`
(`voice.ts`), which reads live `process.env` — the same approach as
`buildSlackAppConfig()` — so per-agent `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` /
`ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` set via `PATCH /agents/{id}/envs` take effect within one
config-sync tick (≤ 60 s) without a restart. Per-agent env wins over
fleet-wide `admin.extraEnv` (config-sync overwrites the process value); when a
per-agent voice key is removed, `revertRemovedVoiceEnv` restores the fleet
value or unsets it, so the agent falls back to Piper on the next tick. Each
synthesis logs `[voice] TTS backend: elevenlabs|piper` (never the key).

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVEL` | `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | Passed to `claude` as `--model`, `--fallback-model`, `--effort`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | 25 min | Idle timeout: restarts on every stdout line. The one that fires in practice. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_MS` | 1 h | Hard ceiling. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL`, `_TOKEN`, `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | unset | Chat poller. |
| `SLACK_ALERT_CHANNEL`, `SLACK_OWNER_USER` | unset | Alert target and the owner used by cron delivery. |

Timeout overrides must be positive integers; anything else falls back to the
default so a bad value never disables the timeout. The environment can also
change after boot: each config sync calls `setLiveClaudeConfig` so the next
spawn picks up new model and tool settings without a restart.

## Running Claude (`claude.ts`)

`createRunClaude(...)` returns `run(message, sessionKey?, onProgress?, signal?,
extraEnv?, onEarlySessionId?)`, which spawns:

```
claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools <FLOOR_TOOLS + live allowedTools> --model ... [-r <sessionId>]
```

- **Tools.** `FLOOR_TOOLS` (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, TodoWrite, Skill) are
  always granted. Everything else, including Bash, comes from the agent's tool
  rows in the config bundle, so an agent with none gets no shell.
- **Serialization.** Calls with the same session key run one after another;
  different keys run concurrently.
- **Resume.** A stored session id is passed with `-r`. If a run fails, it is
  retried once, resuming the same session; the stored id is never cleared and
  no fresh session is started. Abort, idle-timeout and connection-lost
  failures are not retried (a ceiling timeout is). If the retry also fails,
  the original error is rethrown.
- **Errors.** `ClaudeRunError`, `ClaudeTimeoutError` and `ClaudeAbortedError`;
  `reportClaudeError` forwards to Sentry when it is configured.
- **Result.** `ClaudeRunResult` carries the reply text, session id, token usage
  and per-model usage (`dominantModel` picks the one to attribute).

Session ids live in `sessions.ts`: `createFileSessionStore(path)` is a JSON file
keyed by `channel:thread_ts` (`threadKey`), with a per-file write queue so
concurrent set/clear calls cannot lose writes. Entries expire after 7 days and
`startSessionPruner` sweeps every 6 hours. Chat sessions use the key
`chat:<threadId>` in a separate file (`paths.chatSessions`).

## Entry points that call Claude

| Source | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Slack DM, mention, reaction | `slack.ts` | Bolt Socket Mode. Streams progress (`slack-progress.ts`, `progress-milestones.ts`), transcribes voice notes and synthesizes replies (`voice.ts`). Reports chat tokens via `chat-token-reporter.ts`. |
| Chat service | `chat-poller.ts` | Lists threads, claims the next unclaimed user message, runs it, posts the reply. A failure on one thread is logged and the others continue; a failed run must not leave the message claimed forever. |
| Cron | `cron-handler.ts` | `POST /cron` on the health server (and the internal scheduler). Body: `jobId`, `prompt`, optional `channel`, `user`, `silent`, `preCheck`. The prompt is prefixed `[Cron job: <id>] Current time: ...` (Pacific time). |

`POST /cron` returns 400 for bad JSON or a missing `jobId`/`prompt`, 422 for a
`ValidationError` (for example no delivery target), 503 if cron deps are not
wired, 500 for runner errors and 200 on success. Run outcomes go to the admin
API through `cron-run-reporter.ts`; failures are reported once
(`cron-failure-reporter.ts`).

### Reply markers (`markers.ts`)

`parseMarkers` strips these from the reply before it is posted and returns them
as actions: `[silent]`, `[upload:/abs/path]`, `[speak:text]`,
`[react:a,b]`, `[plan:url]`, `[skip-reason:text]`. A malformed marker is logged
and left in the text rather than crashing the run.

## Extension seam (`agent-extension.ts`)

The runtime calls an `AgentExtension` at fixed points; every hook is optional.

| Hook | When |
|---|---|
| `onConfigSync(bundle)` | After each successful config sync. |
| `periodicPasses` | Each reconciler tick; one failing pass is logged and does not stop the rest. |
| `onCronJobs(jobs)` | Each cron sync, before classification. |
| `classifyCronJobs(jobs)` | Chooses which jobs are scheduled, and whether each dispatches as `loop` or `generic`. |
| `dispatchLoop(loopCronId)` | Fires a job classified as `loop`. |

`composeExtensions` merges factories passed to `startAgent`. With none, all
cron jobs are generic and there are no periodic passes. This file must not
import a specialty module; only `index.ts` wires one in.

## GitHub auth and repos

- `github-app-auth.ts` caches installation tokens and refreshes them early.
  `github-installations.ts` tracks the installations, and
  `github-installations-reporter.ts` reports them to the admin API.
- `gh-token-files.ts` writes the token to a file that
  `scripts/bin/git-credential-shipwright.sh` reads through `$GH_TOKEN_FILE`;
  a PAT (`GH_TOKEN`) is the fallback when no App is configured.
- `spawn-env.ts` adds `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER` to loop and cron spawns so the `gh`
  wrapper picks the matching installation token. DM spawns get no hint.
- `sync-config-clone.ts` clones repos that appear in the config, using
  `gh repo clone` through an async spawn so health probes are not blocked.
- `worktree-reaper.ts` force-removes `worktrees/<repo>-<branch>` directories
  older than the configured cleanup age, with no GitHub or task-store calls.

## Health (`health.ts`)

`GET /health` returns `{ok, slack, claudeCodeVersion}`. It returns 500 only when
the Slack socket has been down longer than `SLACK_DOWN_GRACE_MS` (90 s). That
is the self-heal path: a sustained wedge trips the liveness probe and the pod
restarts. Reconnect blips and the not-yet-connected startup window stay 200.

## Tests

Tests sit beside the code as `*.unit.test.ts`, `*.integration.test.ts` and
`*.smoke.test.ts`; shared fixtures are in `runtime/fixtures/`. The
Dockerfile's module-resolution guard and base-image contract are covered by
`base-image-contract.smoke.test.ts`; change them together. Run single files with
`bun test runtime/<file>`.
